items.title: What Is an Agent Harness? How AI Security Tools Work
items.summary: Two AI security tools can use the same model and produce very different results. The difference is the harness. This post explains what an agent harness is, how its execution loop works, and why design choices around context, verification, and scope matter for AI-powered penetration testing.

items.title: AI Findings are Cheap to Find & Costly to Trust
items.summary: AI can produce a plausible vulnerability report in seconds, but proving it is real still takes expert judgment. This post explores the economics of false positives, why they burden your most senior people, and why accountability stays human.

items.title: A Journey into Claude's Sandbox
items.summary: What started as a question about Claude’s sandbox turned into a connected investigation of container internals, process memory, and authorization tokens. Bishop Fox researcher Chris Davis documents what Claude revealed, what it handed over, and what that means for defense in depth.

items.title: Responder Guidance for PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
items.summary: On October 21, 2026, the PHP project disclosed two critical memory-corruption vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Both are fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Every PHP install serving web requests is in scope,

items.title: The True Blast Radius of an AI Attack
items.summary: Connecting AI to enterprise systems changes what organizations entrust software to do. An agent that can query internal databases or modify business records has operational authority, and the scope of that authority becomes a security decision.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.summary: Testing AI security without clear scoping produces superficial coverage and unaddressed risk. This post breaks down how to define boundaries, select the right assessment type, and align AI penetration testing, red teaming, and architecture reviews to the decisions that actually matter.

items.title: Behind Closed Doors: How Physical Penetration Testing Secures Sensitive Conversations
items.summary: Closing the door doesn’t make a room secure. Alethe Denis breaks down how physical penetration testing evaluates whether unauthorized people can reach sensitive spaces, interact with equipment, or leave something behind without anyone noticing or reporting it.

items.title: Submit and Execute: Weaponizing Reflected XSS in Siemens Teamcenter's Login Redirect (CVE-2026-58113)
items.summary: A crafted link, one page load, and no clicks required. Bishop Fox found a reflected XSS in Siemens Teamcenter’s login redirect that auto-submits its own form, turning attribute injection into zero-interaction code execution and a silent surrogate delegation change on the victim’s account.

items.title: Why the AI Attack Surface Extends Your Stack
items.summary: Integrating AI into enterprise applications creates risk across every layer of the stack, not just the model. This post maps the full AI attack surface, shows how a prompt injection can chain into credential theft and cross-tenant data exposure, and explains why isolated scanners miss most of it.

items.title: One Port to Root: Weaponizing Check Point Management CVE-2026-93616
items.summary: An unauthenticated attacker who can reach TCP 19009 on a Check Point management server can take it over completely. Bishop Fox reproduced the full root RCE chain on R81.10 and R82.10, breaks down all three vulnerabilities the patch actually closes, and shares a safe detection tool for defenders.

items.title: Separating Signal from Slop: Triaging CVEs in the Age of AI Security Research
items.summary: AI-assisted research is flooding the CVE pipeline with bugs that score critical but depend on configurations almost nobody runs. Bishop Fox tested four high-profile Nginx CVEs in the lab, measured real-world prevalence, and explains how to separate actual risk from well-marketed noise.

items.title: Zilliz / Attu | 2.6.5
items.summary: Two vulnerabilities in Zilliz Attu 2.6.5 chain into something serious. Missing authentication lets anyone proxy requests unauthenticated, and a regex bypass defeats the private IP block. Bishop Fox turned both into full Kubernetes namespace takeover in a cloud deployment. Update to 3.0.0 now.

items.title: Master Key Included: Detecting SolarWinds ARM CVE-2026-28326
items.summary: A hardcoded authentication secret ships with every SolarWinds Access Rights Manager install, and reaching TCP 55555 is enough to hit a .NET deserialization sink. Bishop Fox confirmed SYSTEM-level code execution, breaks down the root cause, and shares a safe detection tool for defenders.

items.title: Unified Code, Unified Risks: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in .NET MAUI Applications
items.summary: .NET MAUI lets developers write once and ship to both platforms. From an attacker's perspective, that means reverse-engineer once and break everywhere. This post walks through extracting readable assemblies from MAUI apps and the high-impact vulnerability patterns that consistently appear.

items.title: From Fork to Framework: What Modifying Apollo Taught Us About Agent Invasion
items.summary: Forking an existing C2 agent sounds faster than building from scratch. Bishop Fox learned otherwise. This post documents what happened when they forked Apollo, built a 16-pass obfuscation pipeline to defeat EDR detection, and spent months fighting an architecture never designed for it.

items.title: MikroTrick: Inside the RouterOS Takeover Chain
items.summary: Attackers were exploiting MikroTik routers before fixes went public. Bishop Fox reproduced the full unauthenticated takeover chain, found persistence artifacts on real compromised devices, and breaks down what defenders need to investigate beyond patching to confirm they are actually clean.

items.title: CVE-2026-82329: Unauthenticated Administrative Access in JFrog Artifactory via an Empty Cluster Join Key
items.summary: A misconfigured cluster join key in JFrog Artifactory's default install lets unauthenticated attackers mint a permanent admin token in one request. Bishop Fox reproduced the full chain, confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, and shares a non-invasive detection check and remediation guidance.

items.title: Mind the Config: Detecting and Weaponizing NetScaler CVE-2026-19490
items.summary: A single unauthenticated request bypasses authentication on NetScaler Gateway and AAA virtual servers. Whether that means a dead-end session, a proxy into the internal network, or root on the appliance depends entirely on configuration. Bishop Fox maps every branch and shares a safe detection tool.

items.title: Signature Optional - Analysis of CVE-2026-28323
items.summary: SolarWinds Web Help Desk treated SAML signature verification as optional and skipped every other validation the spec requires. Bishop Fox confirmed the full exploit end to end: one forged POST request, no credentials, full session takeover. Here is the root cause, the fix, and how to detect it.

items.title: Traefik | Version Through 3.7.11
items.summary: Traefik's request read timeout is enabled by default and documented without exception, but it has never applied to HTTP/3. Bishop Fox confirmed the gap across four years of releases, measured it against the backend, and reported it to the vendor, who shipped a fix within twelve days.
